Rogue Paramedic

By: Hein Kaiser | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
we investigate how first responders to an incident can cost you your life.

Unique Selling Point:
We meet and see how Reinette van der Heever puts lives at danger while feeding her narcicisstic tendencies to exploit accidents and incidents, and post it for her 'fans' on TikTok

Summary:
It’s a response to the scarce emergency services resources.

The community of Brakpan is one of these communities where several civic organisations, private security companies and volunteers along with the local chaplaincy have stepped in to fill the gap where services are simply not available or take way too long to respond.

Members of the community underwent their own, self funded training and many of them are fully qualified first responders, who manage a scene or try and save lives within the protocols that they are qualified in, until government agencies arrive on the scene. Or if they do at all.

We investigate this growing phenomenon, and see how communities are stepping in and saving lives. But in some instances, allowing people to die, because they operate illegally.

What happens when some community members turn into “911 Vigilantes” as we would call them?


Further information:
Reinette vd Heever runs a band of ‘vigilante’ first responders under a WhatsApp group called Brakpan First Responders. In this group, separate to the rest of the community, she calls the shots and, in some cases, decides who lives and dies.

Reinette’s husband and son are in this endeavour with her, and arrive at incident scenes in their now notorious blue polo, complete and illegally kitted out with red or blue lights, depending on the emergency. (when we film the community, she is bound to pop up at an incident)

Reinette only has has a basic first aid training certificate, she is not even legally allowed to dispense a Panado.

Or is there something additional at play here – her TikTok channel streams every single accident, she films hurt people and private information and publishes it. Word is, she enjoys sponsorship for all of this, too….

LOCATION SCRIPT
COLLAGE AND SOUNDS OF tik toks at accident scenes transitioning into visuals of adults playing with toy cars.

INTRO VO

South Africa’s reputation for road safety is anything but stellar. One of the highest accident rates in the world makes driving here anything but child’s play.

SPLIT VO
But for those involved in accidents in Brakpan, on Jo’burg’s East Rand, survival becomes a lottery.

GLORIA
There was an incident where two first responders from different groups were arguing on scene about who's scene it was and not paying any attention to the patient like they should be. And the patient's had a cardiac arrest and stopped breathing, basically was dead.
VO

A first responder is someone who gets to a scene of an emergency, like a car accident, first.

It’s also a term used by community members who ‘help out’ and arrive on a scene as good samaritans, ostensibly to save lives.

They are neither paramedics nor ambulance drivers - but usually
members of the community with limited training - and they respond to medical emergencies.

UPSOUND STAN
They love to go out. They love the hype. They love all the red lights and the blue lights. It kind of drives them and motivates them to go there and to try to provide some kind of assistance.
PAUSE
VO

For some first responders, it’s a weekend hobby to monitor community social groups and cruise the streets, looking for the thrill of saving a life and chatting about it online.

For others, it’s a round-the-clock calling??

VO

Reinette van der Heever has been a full-time community volunteer for several years…painting old age homes, caring for the underprivileged. She is also an Advanced Level three responder, and responds to about 25 incidents every month.
REINETTE
[We do fire and rescue and in the ice and vice versa. There is now motor vehicle accidents, motorbike accidents, pedestrian accidents.
VO

With provincial emergency services sometimes taking hours to get to a scene, community first responders like Reinette fulfil an important role.

She’s a member of one of nine different volunteer groups in Brakpan.
MAC
The WhatsApp groups? Are they community based WhatsApp groups or is it just mainly for responders?
REINETTE
It's responders because there’s patient confidentiality and there’s an ILS, which is intermediate life support, which gives assistance to us on the groups.
VO
But all isn't as it seems. An advanced first responder, as Reinette calls herself, is qualified to deal with workplace emergencies.
MIKE

It doesn't give them the authority to respond to a call. That's why we have emergency services. They're trying to do good, but by doing good, they're doing bad.
VO
Are first responders crossing a line?

In addition to emergency care, Medicare24 CEO Mike van Wyk specialises in medical law.

MAC
How dangerous is this for a victim?
MIKE
They're responding with red lights and sirens to an incident and in a taking over the scene and they're starting to manage that patient, they can't do it
It's against the law.

and that puts them in huge, huge danger.




VO

We joined Reinette and crew for a night out.

Former fireman Louis Pretorius, a qualified intermediate life support medic, joins them as a volunteer,



MAC
Are you finding that there's not enough emergency services or the response is not quick enough?
LOUIS

Actually, both in a bit more. There is a designated service in town. They've got limited capacity.

VO

Are they right to pick up the slack left by provincial emergency services?



LINK

They hang out in places like this all night waiting for distress calls.
STAN
If they are not trained and officially qualified, they literally introduce a risk to society.
VO

Stan Bezuidenhout is a forensic accident investigator and has led thousands of incident inquiries.

MAC [
So right now we have an issue where people are just arriving at accident scenes and there's no one regulating the space.
STAN
Not only accident scenes, even crime scenes, even shooting incidents, even cash in transit, robberies, bombings.somebody arrived at one of these cash in transit scenes where they responded to an active shooting incident where the person arrive with a paint ball gun and said, Where do you want to deploy me? Where you deploy a guy with a paintball gun..
STAN
And unfortunately, you always have to say is the is the possible benefit outweighed by the possible harm? Obviously it's better to have somebody who cares enough to try then to have situations where people stand by or they are just too scared to try because it is regulation.
VO
Reinette has a boot full of first aid equipment, ready for action at any time.
And when something happens, she hauls out more than just bandages.
Reinette films every scene and posts them to social media, recording her good deeds for likes and follows, and for what she calls….. marketing.
….for first responder groups in Brakpan, helping people has become a competitive business
LOUIS
Somewhere somehow this entitlement of it's my patient was born.

VO
Jostling for the moral high ground has even gone to court.
Reinette and a competing responder obtained restraining orders against each other.
What would happen if they respond to the same accident… yet they cannot be near each other.
Who gets to save the life…
MAC
Is there turf war, though?
REINETTE
We know we don't really have that issues. I don't have those problems.
VO
Reinette started sharing….
She said that there are ‘other’ competing responders who arrive at scenes intoxicated and then transport victims in unregistered, home-made ambulances.
…..a first responder is not even allowed to dispense a headache tablet, yet Reinette says that there are some volunteers who even puncture skin to insert drips and administer medication.
VO

Once a first responder herself, Gloria lost enthusiasm for it. She says it became about ego and social media likes.

This has led to first responders overstepping the mark, making life and death decisions…






GLORIA
There has been a few cases where first responders have declared or told don't resus. The patients are about to die from injuries us which is basically killing the patient
There's been a few times where the first responders have declared patients p4
VO
A call they’re not legally permitted to make.
GLORIA
[00:26:33] there was a time when. Renette, Declared a patient and said, don't resuscitate anymore. Patients gone. You might as well stop doing chest compressions,

VO
Someone with a first aid qualification cannot declare anyone’s death. That should be left to professionals who can detect signs of life…or not.
VO
We spoke to another former first responder who made claims about an incident where Reinette was present. Like Gloria, he wanted us to hide his identity
VO
Our source was a good samaritan trying to save a man’s life during a heart attack.
Then Reinette and other first responders arrived on the scene.
SOURCE AUDIO
I just keep on of the compressions on the chestI think it was about 45 minutes, They arrived and just stood there.
They told me to stop the compressions.
VO
The patient died.
Reinette denied that our source was told to stop the compressions.
But it doesn't end there. In this cauldron of potentially fatal injuries and competing interests, Reinette partners with… her son.

REINETTE
He treats patients under my supervision.
VO
Her son is 15.. He has his own responder badge.
His first aid qualification allows him to patch someone up with a plaster at a school rugby match…

But he does much more than that on a scene….

Change voice
Beep out Dylan
“Voice of another first responder” SOURCE AUDIO
Dylan was there, her son, she was standing by the, the child, the force the way she was. Yeah. And then he said he's got a laceration to the knee and, and the concussion.
VO


In other words, while out with mom, Reinette’s son made a roadside diagnosis of an accident victim and listed lacerations and a concussion as injuries.


MIKE
That kid has no right to treat a patient in any form or any way when it comes to an accident scene on the road. He's putting his own life in danger, number one. Number two, now he's putting people's lives in danger.
VO
On the night we spent with Reinette….. her son told us that he has been to many horrific accident scenes.

Reinette thinks its ok.
REINETTE
He’s are actually more clever than me with patients. Yes.
MAC
Are patients comfortable though, I see a 15 year old at an accident I’m gonna be…
REINETTE
They love him. And even the people from the ambulances, they love him
VO

Our night in Brakpan shows there's a danger of no good deed going unpunished

MIKE
[03:38:08] I think they need to stop immediately. And if they go through the proper training
[03:39:47] That's the only way you can resolve this. It's bordering on criminal, if not already at the criminal level at this point of time.

metadata.Summary: It’s a response to the scarce emergency services resources. The community of Brakpan is one of these communities where several civic organisations, private security companies and volunteers along with the local chaplaincy have stepped in to fill the gap where services are simply not available or take way too long to respond. Members of the community underwent their own, self funded training and many of them are fully qualified first responders, who manage a scene or try and save lives within the protocols that they are qualified in, until government agencies arrive on the scene. Or if they do at all. We investigate this growing phenomenon, and see how communities are stepping in and saving lives. But in some instances, allowing people to die, because they operate illegally. What happens when some community members turn into “911 Vigilantes” as we would call them?
metadata.Further information: Reinette vd Heever runs a band of ‘vigilante’ first responders under a WhatsApp group called Brakpan First Responders. In this group, separate to the rest of the community, she calls the shots and, in some cases, decides who lives and dies. Reinette’s husband and son are in this endeavour with her, and arrive at incident scenes in their now notorious blue polo, complete and illegally kitted out with red or blue lights, depending on the emergency. (when we film the community, she is bound to pop up at an incident) Reinette only has has a basic first aid training certificate, she is not even legally allowed to dispense a Panado. Or is there something additional at play here – her TikTok channel streams every single accident, she films hurt people and private information and publishes it. Word is, she enjoys sponsorship for all of this, too….
